what: resolveId's raw-hash tolerance — an old account hash accepted where a pubid is now the wire id
pattern: SELECT hash FROM profiles WHERE hash = \?1 LIMIT 1'\)\.bind\(wire\)
how: once every shared `profile.html?u=<hash>` link and push `?dm=<hash>` URL minted before the L3 flip has aged out (30 days), drop resolveId's trailing raw-hash lookup so only a pubid resolves; an account hash on the wire is then simply unknown. — moved from 2026-10-18 on 2026-10-19: the same lookup is also the net for a member registered after the reverse map loaded (lib.ts resolveId), so retiring it needs a `pubid = ?1` lookup in its place, an identity change for its own pull request and /security-review, not a line deleted under a red build.

what: weakKeyTolerated — a WEAK identity key that already has history behind it may still write
how: delete weakKeyTolerated() and the `known && weakKeyTolerated()` clause in keyFloor, so the floor holds for EVERY write. A weak-key member is no longer locked out: key rotation (POST /profile/rekey, 2026-09-18) lets them move to a strong key with their content, so on the due date a weak key is refused a write and told to rotate. Run scripts/key_audit.py first and give any cracked member a heads-up to rotate; move this date only if one cannot be reached in time. — moved from 2026-10-18 on 2026-10-19: scripts/key_audit.py has not been run and no weak-key member has had the heads-up yet; both come first.

what: the legacy actor_hash clause: a DM bell from before 0016 named its sender, not its thread
how: once no unread bell with topic_id 0 remains, drop this clause and the two `topic_id = 0 AND actor_hash` clauses in routes/dm.ts; tests/worker/notif_read — moved from 2026-10-16 on 2026-10-17: two unread pre-0016 DM bells (topic_id 0) still stood in production, and this clause is what clears them when their conversation is read; retire it once none remains (or once they are marked read).
